key_insight: DocTalk’s chart-grounded instruction tuning improved medical question-answering performance across six open-source language models.
clinical_relevance: The system could help clinicians retrieve information from discharge summaries, but the abstract does not establish benefits for patient care.
method: Generated 500 QA pairs from de-identified discharge summaries using sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review.
Evaluated three general-purpose and three biomedical models before and after LoRA instruction tuning.
Tested the two best-performing models on PubMedQA for external generalization.
evidence_signal: The best tuned model achieved ROUGE-L 0.40, BERTScore-F1 0.76, and UMLS-F1 0.49; PubMedQA accuracy improved from 93.1% to 97.7% and 93.5% to 94.3% for the two evaluated models.
watch_item: The small, generated QA dataset and benchmark results do not establish real-world clinical safety or reliable hallucination control.
paper_title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
